subject: Belgium
note: Cited to a pinned Wikipedia revision (trusted_secondary): Baarle-Hertog. The street plan and the municipality's outline are OpenStreetMap data (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL); the outline is the Belgian municipality of Baarle-Hertog, so the gaps in it are Dutch land.

claims.text: Baarle-Hertog has 22 Belgian exclaves fully within the Netherlands.
There are seven Dutch enclaves within the Belgian exclaves.
Some houses in the town of Baarle-Hertog/Baarle-Nassau are divided between the two countries.
At one time restaurants in the Netherlands had to close earlier than those in Belgium, so customers moved to a table on the Belgian side.
The border's complexity results from medieval treaties, agreements, land-swaps and sales, ratified under the Treaty of Maastricht in 1843.
